skill.name: writing-data
skill.description: Guides modular data file organization for a Next.js app data folder.
skill.summary: Structure Next.js app data into small, modular files.
skill.author: Emz1998

security_audit.summary: The two static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline-code backticks around srs/data in SKILL.md. I found no executable code, shell invocation instructions, prompt injection text, or semantic data-exfiltration intent in the 16-line skill file.

static_findings.snippet: description: Use this skill when you need to structure data in `srs/data` for the Next.js app
- Follow the rules below to structure data in `srs/data` for the Next.js app:

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 3 uses Markdown backticks to format the literal path srs/data in frontmatter text. It does not instruct or execute Ruby, shell, or any command.
Line 8 uses Markdown backticks to format the literal path srs/data in an instruction sentence. It does not contain command execution or user-controlled shell input.

content.value_statement: App data files can become hard to maintain when unrelated records are grouped together. This skill gives simple rules for modular Next.js data files.
actual_capabilities: States that data should be organized inside the app data folder.
Requires modular organization for data files.
Sets a 50-line maximum for each file.
Directs users to split data into multiple files when possible.
Prefers one data item per file.
limitations: It does not define a complete data schema for the application.
It does not provide validation, build scripts, or automated file generation.
It only gives organization rules for app data files.
It cannot verify whether the target folder exists without project context.

use_cases.title: Organize Feature Data
use_cases.description: Plan small data files for a new Next.js feature without creating oversized files.

use_cases.title: Split Content Records
use_cases.description: Separate repeatable site content into focused files for easier updates.

use_cases.title: Review Data Structure
use_cases.description: Check a proposed data folder against simple size and modularity rules.

prompt_templates.title: Place A New Data Item
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the writing-data skill to place this new item in the app data folder. Make one file for one data item.

prompt_templates.title: Split Several Items
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the writing-data skill to split these related items into modular data files. Keep every file under 50 lines.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Large Data File
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the writing-data skill to review this large data file plan. Propose smaller files with one data item per file.

prompt_templates.title: Audit A Data Folder Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the writing-data skill to check my proposed app data folder structure. Identify files that break modularity or 50-line rules.

output_examples.input: A request to add two testimonials and one pricing item to the app data folder.
output_examples.output: A file plan with separate testimonial files and a separate pricing file, each under 50 lines.

output_examples.input: A large content data file that mixes navigation, pricing, and testimonials.
output_examples.output: A restructuring recommendation that separates each content area into focused data files.

output_examples.input: A proposed folder plan for several feature data items.
output_examples.output: A review that flags oversized files and grouped records that should be split.

best_practices: Keep each file focused on one data item or closely related record.
Split data before a file approaches 50 lines.
Use clear file names that match the data they contain.
anti_patterns: Do not group unrelated data only to reduce file count.
Do not create files that exceed the 50-line rule.
Do not treat the skill as a replacement for schema validation.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps organize Next.js app data into small, modular files.

faq.question: Does it define a data schema?
faq.answer: No. It gives file organization rules, not field-level schema requirements.

faq.question: Can it create data files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance. Your AI tool may edit files when you request changes.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill reports support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What is the main file size rule?
faq.answer: Each data file should stay under 50 lines.

faq.question: When should data be split?
faq.answer: Split data when multiple records or unrelated items can live in separate files.
